maria.k: Heads up — spotted a rendering quirk on the KB page https://kb.redwood.internal/guides/embed-widgets. Legacy embed wrappers that use HTML comment markers are swallowing fenced code blocks after the new renderer rolled out. sam: Can you paste a minimal example? I want to repro locally. :eyes: maria.k: Minimal snippet (copied from the page): ```html 
function greet() {
  console.log("hi");
}
``` When this lands in the new renderer the inner fenced/code content doesn't show — it just disappears (no syntax highlighting). Staging shows the same. jon: Hmm. That looks like the parser treats the whole comment-block as raw HTML and strips inner markup. New renderer likely runs an HTML sanitizer before code block parsing. sam: Quick check — if you replace the wrapper with a shortcode style it renders? e.g.: ```md {{< legacy-embed id="legacy-snippet" >}} ``` maria.k: I tried that in a local branch and triple backticks do render, yes. But we have ~12 pages still using the old comment wrappers. sam: I can open a small PR to replace the wrappers with the shortcode on that page and add a tiny unit test to prevent regressions. Who owns the page? Frontmatter shows `owner: docs-content` which is a group, not a person. jon: I actually own that section — frontmatter was set weirdly during the migration. Feel free to assign the PR to me. If it's a mechanical replace we can bulk-fix other pages too. maria.k: Awesome. If you want, start with this page and then run the grep/replace for `
